ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $ \triangle ABC$, $ \angle C=90^\circ$, O is a point on side AB, circle $O$ is tangent to both AC and BC. If $ BC=3$ and $ AC=4$, what is the radius of circle $O$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct OD$\perp$AC at D, OE$\perp$BC at E, as shown in the figure, let the radius of $\odot O$ be $r$,\\
since $\odot O$ is tangent to both AC and BC,\\
thus OD=OE=r,\\
and $\angle C=90^\circ$,\\
thus quadrilateral ODCE is a square,\\
thus CD=OD=r,\\
since OD$\parallel$BC,\\
thus $\triangle ADO\sim \triangle ACB$,\\
thus $\frac{AF}{AC}=\frac{OF}{BC}$ \\
since AF=AC−r, BC=3, AC=4,\\
substituting in, we get $\frac{4−r}{4}=\frac{r}{3}$\\
thus $r=\boxed{\frac{12}{7}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure is a right triangle ABC, C is at the lower left, AC is the vertical side, BC is the horizontal side, AB is the hypotenuse; point O is marked on the hypotenuse AB, and the circle with O as center is tangent to both the vertical side AC and the horizontal side BC. The problem gives BC=3, AC=4. Reasoning: According to the specified coordinate method, take the right-angle vertex C as the origin, place BC on the positive x-axis and AC on the positive y-axis, then C=(0,0), B=(3,0), A=(0,4). Let the radius of the circle be r. Because the circle is tangent to both coordinate axes AC and BC, the distances from the center to the x-axis and y-axis are both equal to r, so O=(r,r). Also because the figure and the problem statement give that O is on side AB, (r,r) satisfies the equation of line AB. The equation of the line through A=(0,4) and B=(3,0) is x/3 + y/4 = 1, that is, 4x+3y=12. Substituting x=y=r gives 4r+3r=12, that is, 7r=12, so r=12/7.
